I want a simple sign-out log for the shared camera and sound kit in our video team. There are six of us. Someone takes a camera out for a shoot, and a week later nobody knows who has it. People should see what kit we have, sign an item out, sign it back in, and see who has what right now. Nothing exists yet, we would be starting fresh.

Thank you. That is clear. I recorded it.

One honest note first. For six people, a shared spreadsheet could do this job. It needs one row for each item, with a "Who has it" column and a "Since" date. A short form can add to the spreadsheet when someone signs an item out. It costs nothing and you can start it today. A custom tool helps more if you want a fixed rule, for example "you cannot sign out an item that someone already has", or a clean history that nobody can change by accident. If you want the custom tool, I continue with it. I wrote the spreadsheet option in the notes and will not ask about it again.

**Question 2:** When someone signs an item out, how does the tool know who that person is?

My guess: there is no password. Each person picks their name from a list of the six team…

It is only for the six of us, nobody outside the team. Each person should sign in with their work email, so the log shows who took what. It keeps names, work emails and the list of kit, nothing else. There is no money, no customers, no health or personal data, and nothing happens automatically. If it is down for a day we go back to the whiteboard in the kit room.

Good. I recorded this: six people only, sign-in with work email, and the tool keeps only names, work emails and the kit list. There is no money, no customer data and no automatic action. If the tool stops for a day, the team uses the whiteboard. This tells me the risk is low.

**Question 3:** Who may add new kit to the list, change an item, or remove an item, for example a camera that broke or was sold?

My guess: any of the six can add or change an item. You do not need one person in charge of the list. Is that right?
Anyone can sign any item out or back in, and anyone can add new kit to the list. We are one small team, so that is fine.

Recorded. Anyone of the six can sign any item out or back in, also an item that another person took out. Anyone can add new kit.

**Question 4:** What happens when an item leaves the team for good, for example a microphone that broke or was sold?

My guess: anyone can mark the item as "retired". It then goes off the main list, but its past sign-outs stay in the history. This way the record of who had it does not go away. Is that right?

We would open it in a web browser, on laptops and on our phones, and it has to work when my laptop is off. We have no server of our own and nobody who looks after one. I am happy to own any accounts it needs.

Thank you. I recorded this: the team opens the tool in a web browser on laptops and phones. It must run on a hosted service, not on your laptop. You will own the accounts.

You did not answer Question 4 about retiring an item, so I use my guess for now: anyone can mark an item "retired", it goes off the main list, and its history stays. You can change this later.

**Question 5:** Which service gives your team its work email? Sign-in with work email works through this service.

- **Google Workspace** (Gmail with your company name) ← my guess
- **Microsoft 365** (Outlook with your company name)
